title: Google scan of Common Crawl finds malicious web prompt injections aimed at AI readers up 32 percent, mostly low sophistication
summary: Google scanned Common Crawl snapshots of 2-3 billion pages with pattern matching, Gemini-based intent classification and manual validation, and reports a relative increase of 32 percent in the malicious category of web prompt injections between November 2025 and February 2026. Most hits were tone-changing pranks, SEO text steering AI assistants toward one business, pages deterring AI agents including one that streams endless text to waste resources, and a few low-sophistication exfiltration and file-deletion attempts judged unlikely to succeed; Google expects scale and sophistication to grow and names red teams, its AI Vulnerability Reward Program and real-time threat filtering as responses.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; page dated Apr 23, 2026, authors Thomas Brunner, Yu-Han Liu and Moni Pande; the 32 percent relative increase, the Common Crawl three-stage method and the category list confirmed from the article body. Candidate title said 'four months'; the page gives only the endpoints November 2025 and February 2026, so the title was reworded.
